links.outcome: Fairness (GEO) and AUROC of SDoH-aware vs SDoH-unaware glaucoma progression models
links.effect: SDoH-aware model lowered GEO in internal set (0.098 vs 0.216) and mixed-population site (0.172 vs 0.378) with negligible AUROC change; no improvement at rural high-DCI site (0.241 vs 0.228).
links.quote: Incorporating SDoH features can improve algorithmic fairness regarding socioeconomic disparities without sacrificing predictive accuracy; however, these benefits do not universally transfer to external sites with demographically dissimilar cohorts.

links.outcome: Model fairness metrics across socioeconomic subgroups and external sites
links.effect: Fairness (GEO) varied by site: improved internally (0.098 vs 0.216) and at mixed-population site (0.172 vs 0.378), marginal at urban site (0.491 vs 0.504), none at rural site (0.241 vs 0.228).
links.quote: AI models require rigorous external validation across diverse populations to ensure equity prior to clinical implementation.

links.outcome: Fairness benefit transfer to external sites with demographically dissimilar cohorts
links.effect: Fairness gains did not generalize to a highly urbanized low-DCI site (0.491 vs 0.504) or a rural high-DCI site (0.241 vs 0.228).
links.quote: However, fairness benefits did not universally generalize to demographically dissimilar external cohorts.

screen.reason: Evaluates the impact and generalizability of incorporating community-level SDoH features to mitigate algorithmic bias across external validation sites.

primary.practice: inclusion of social determinants of health to improve fairness across sites
